transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because I keep having these nagging thoughts that I’ve forgotten something important. Like, I’ll worry I left my aunt’s medicine out the wrong way, or that I didn’t set up my classroom materials safely. Even when I know I probably handled it, the doubt just keeps coming back into my head.
Do you find yourself doing anything over and over to try and get rid of these nagging thoughts?

Yes. Before I leave the house or my classroom, I’ll go back and check the same things a few times. Like the pill organizer, the stove, my lesson plans… sometimes I’ll also just replay in my head what I did. I usually keep doing it until I feel calm enough to move on, but it can make me late sometimes.
Do you feel anxious when you have these nagging thoughts?

Yes, I do. It’s like this anxious doubt that pops up, even when I know I probably did things right. I’ll think maybe I left my aunt’s medicine out wrong, or maybe something in my classroom isn’t safe, and then I can’t really relax until I feel sure.
Do you feel like checking things over and over helps reduce your anxiety?

Yes, it does, at least for a little while. If I go back and check the pill organizer or the stove, or look over my lesson plans again, I feel calmer afterward. Sometimes I’ll also replay what I did in my head until it feels okay. But it can take a few times, and then I end up running late.
Do you have any recurring thoughts or urges that aren't related to your anxiety about forgetting something or making a mistake?

Not really, no. The main thoughts are about feeling like I forgot something important or set something up wrong—like my aunt’s medicine or something in my classroom not being safe. Even when I know I probably did it right, the doubt just keeps coming back.
Are you checking things over and over because you're trying to prevent something bad from happening, or is it just to feel less anxious?

I think it’s kind of both, but mostly I’m trying to make sure nothing bad happens. Like before I leave the house or my classroom, I’ll go back and check the pill organizer, the stove, or my lesson plans a few times. Sometimes I’ll just replay what I did in my head until it feels okay. Once I feel sure enough, I can move on, but it does make me late sometimes.
Do you feel like you have to perform these checking rituals in a specific way or order to feel calm?

Yeah, sort of. It’s not like a strict order every single time, but I do feel like I have to go back over the same things before I can leave. I’ll check the pill organizer, the stove, or my lesson plans, or I’ll replay what I did in my head until it feels calm enough to move on. Sometimes that means doing it a few times, and then I end up running late.
Do you feel like these thoughts and checking behaviors are interfering with your daily life or relationships?

Yeah, a little. I’m still getting to work and taking care of family stuff, so it’s not like I can’t function, but it does slow me down. My mornings take longer, and sometimes I get to school already feeling rushed or behind. And things like lesson prep or journaling at night don’t feel as smooth or relaxing as they used to.
Do you feel like these thoughts and checking behaviors are causing you a lot of distress?

Yeah, it does bother me. I wouldn’t say it’s overwhelming all the time, but it’s stressful when I feel stuck checking the same things before I can leave. Like I’ll go back over the pill organizer, the stove, or my lesson plans, or replay what I did in my head until I feel calm enough. It’s frustrating because I know it makes me run late sometimes.
Are these thoughts and checking behaviors affecting your relationships with family, friends, or colleagues?

A little, but not in a huge way. I’m still keeping up with work and family commitments, but my mornings take longer, so I sometimes get to school already feeling rushed or behind. And at home, things like lesson prep or my evening journaling don’t feel as smooth or as calming as they used to.
Do you have any thoughts that keep repeating in your mind and are not about forgetting something or making a mistake?
Not really, no. The ones I notice are mostly tied to checking whether I forgot something or did something wrong. I can’t think of other repeated thoughts that come up in the same way.
Do you have any habits or actions that you feel compelled to do over and over that aren't related to checking things?

Not really outside of that. The things I feel pushed to repeat are the checking things—like before I leave the house or my classroom, I’ll go back over the pill organizer, the stove, my lesson plans, or replay what I did in my head a few times until I feel settled enough to go. It’s mostly that, and it can make me late sometimes.
Are there any areas of your life where you feel like these thoughts and checking behaviors are holding you back or causing problems that we haven't talked about yet?

I think it’s mostly what I mentioned before. I’m still doing what I need to do at work and with my family, but the checking makes mornings take longer, and I sometimes get to school already feeling rushed or like I’m behind before the day has even started. And at home, lesson planning and journaling in the evening just don’t feel as easy or calming as they used to.
Are these thoughts and checking behaviors significantly affecting your ability to enjoy or perform daily activities?

Yes, somewhat. I’m still able to get through work and take care of family things, but it slows me down. Mornings take longer than they should, and sometimes I get to school already feeling rushed or like I’m behind before the day even starts. And in the evenings, things like lesson prep or journaling don’t feel as smooth or relaxing as they used to.
Do you feel like these thoughts and checking behaviors are causing you significant distress or impairment in your daily life?

Yes, I’d say it’s distressing, but not completely taking over. I’m still getting through work and family commitments. It’s more that my mornings take longer than they should, and sometimes I get to school already feeling rushed or behind before the day even starts. And at night, lesson prep or journaling just doesn’t feel as smooth or calming as it used to.
Are you having trouble meeting your responsibilities at work or at home because of these thoughts and checking behaviors?

Not exactly trouble meeting them, no. I’m still getting my work done and keeping up with things at home. It’s more that it takes extra time and energy. My mornings get dragged out, and sometimes I get to school feeling rushed or already behind. And in the evenings, lesson planning or journaling just doesn’t feel as smooth or helpful as it used to.
Are you finding it harder to enjoy time with friends or family because of these thoughts and checking behaviors?

A little, yes. I’m still spending time with my family and keeping up with things, but I feel more rushed and less settled, especially after mornings that take too long. By the evening, I can be kind of worn out, and things like lesson prep or journaling don’t feel as relaxing as they used to, so I’m not always as present as I’d like to be.
Are you avoiding social activities or interactions with others because of these thoughts and checking behaviors?

I wouldn’t say I’m really avoiding people or social things. I’m still going to work and doing family commitments. It’s more that I feel rushed or behind sometimes, especially if my morning takes too long, and by evening I’m just less settled. So lesson prep or journaling doesn’t feel as calming as it used to, but I’m not really skipping social interactions because of it.
